rationale: The Living Room Cam (CAM-I2) showed RSSI -84 dBm, below the -80 dBm threshold that causes intermittent disconnections, while all other devices remained online and the base station itself was healthy. The customer's relocation of the base station into the study (further from the camera, with more walls) coincided with the symptom onset. The standard fix — moving the base station back to the hallway — resolved the issue, with the camera staying online all day.

repair_steps: Confirm the base station is back in the hallway and the Living Room Cam has stayed online for at least 24 hours.
Check the Living Room Cam's RSSI in Device Settings > Device Info; if it is now above -80 dBm (ideally above -70 dBm), the signal issue is resolved.
If the customer cannot find RSSI, verify the camera remains online without drops for a full day.
Advise the customer to keep the base station in a central location with minimal walls/obstacles between it and the camera.
If the issue recurs or RSSI remains below -80 dBm, recommend installing an RP-1 repeater or repositioning the camera/base station.
Close the case as resolved at frontline.
output.customer_reply: Thank you for your patience. I'm glad the camera has stayed online after moving the base station back to the hallway. To ensure a stable connection, please keep the base station in a central location with minimal walls between it and the camera. If you experience any further drops, let us know and we can explore adding a signal repeater. Have a great day!

results.text: Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.

complaint: My living room camera keeps going offline a few times a day, then comes back by itself. The other devices seem fine. It started about a week ago, around when we rearranged the flat and I moved the base station into the study to free up a socket in the hallway. I've restarted the camera several times and checked that it is plugged in properly. My partner thinks the camera is faulty and wants to return it, but I'd rather not buy anything new if I can avoid it.

It avoids claiming unperformed checks as completed. Minor weakness: it includes internal repair steps like 'Close the case as resolved at frontline' and some redundancy, but the customer-facing reply is appropriate and does not overclaim.
